articles.title: Researchers find AI spontaneously develops a sense of facial beauty without training
articles.summary: New research shows that artificial neural networks can spontaneously develop a sense of facial beauty without any prior training. This discovery suggests that aesthetic preferences might stem from the basic ways our brains process visual information.

articles.title: More time spent playing video games is linked to a thinner cerebral cortex in adolescents
articles.summary: A study of over 5,600 teenagers links video gaming to differences in brain structure, like a thinner cerebral cortex. However, these associations vary depending on whether adolescents engage in solo, social, or mature-rated gaming.

articles.title: A longer exhale may push your brain toward bolder decisions
articles.summary: Slow breathing with a prolonged exhale made people more willing to take risks by changing heart activity and increasing the brain’s sensitivity to rewards. The findings suggest that something as simple as controlling your breath can directly influence how you evaluate choices.

articles.title: Scientists reveal the hidden instructions that build the human brain
articles.summary: UCLA researchers have discovered two powerful influences that help guide how the human brain forms before birth. Radial glia, stem cells responsible for producing much of the cerebral cortex, change their behavior depending on how they process glucose and on physical contact with signals arriving from the thalamus. Those signals can alter which types of neurons are produced, including upper-layer neurons that are especially prominent in humans.

articles.title: This lifestyle program improved cognition 55% more than basic health advice
articles.summary: Older adults at risk of dementia improved their memory and thinking after following lifestyle programs combining exercise, healthy eating, cognitive training, and social engagement. Those who received regular coaching and structured support improved substantially more than participants given general health advice.

articles.title: Cannabis use alters how the human brain processes nicotine, new research suggests
articles.summary: Recent cannabis use might make higher doses of nicotine feel more unpleasant, according to new research. Scientists discovered that cannabis alters our subjective reaction to the drug without necessarily changing how much we want it.

articles.title: Higher intelligence might accelerate the development of metacognitive knowledge in mathematics
articles.summary: A new study of 1,050 German students reveals that higher intelligence accelerates the development of metacognitive knowledge in math. While girls also outpaced boys, initial math skills and motivation did not affect how quickly this knowledge grew.

articles.title: Struggling to find “the one”? A new psychology study says the problem might be your underlying motivation
articles.summary: A new study suggests that your underlying reasons for wanting a relationship shape the kind of partner you seek. While dating for genuine connection leads to high-quality goals, dating for validation can actually sabotage your romantic success.

articles.title: How chemical tags on a dopamine gene are linked to teen creativity
articles.summary: Researchers have found a link between chemical modifications on a dopamine-related gene and creative thinking abilities in adolescent males. The findings offer early clues into how the environment might biologically shape cognitive development.

articles.title: How cognitive shortcuts fuel American political divisions
articles.summary: When voters clash over public policy, their mutual dislike is driven by how recognizable and organized their beliefs are. A new study finds that structured, consistent political views fuel much deeper animosity than moderate or mixed opinions.

articles.summary: arXiv:2609.04239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This technical report presents EXAONE Forecast for Finance (EXAONE Finance), a financial time series (TS) foundation model (TSFM) tailored to financial forecasting. Recent TSFMs achieve strong zero-shot performance through large-scale pretraining. articles.title: From Matching Models to Recruiting Agents: A Systematized Narrative Review of AI Recruitment Systems, Evaluation, and Governance
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.04286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence in recruitment has shifted the object being automated from profile pairs and ranked lists to multi-stage workflows that retrieve evidence, compare candidates, and support or execute actions. This systematized narrative review traces that development from bilateral retrieval and behavioral ranking through neural person--job matching, large language model (LLM) components, and tool-using recruiting agents. Using a purposive search and coding protocol updated through 23 July 2026, plus targeted updates through 2 September 202
